lead.headline: OCC grants preliminary national bank charter to onchain settlement startup OpenReserve, backed by a16z
lead.tldr: The boundary between crypto-native infrastructure and regulated banking continues to dissolve as OpenReserve's OCC approval signals that onchain settlement is being underwritten as a core banking function, not a peripheral experiment. Meanwhile, institutional ETF accumulation and celebrity DeFi endorsements are repricing what 'mainstream adoption' means for investors.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the regulatory and institutional signals this week are repricing how we underwrite infrastructure versus application-layer bets.

top_signals.title: Andreessen Horowitz-backed OpenReserve secures preliminary OCC approval for national bank charter
top_signals.summary: OpenReserve Holdings has received preliminary approval from the OCC for a national bank charter focused on onchain settlement. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz and recently completed a seed funding round.
top_signals.why_it_matters: This is the clearest signal yet that US regulators are willing to charter crypto-native banks for core settlement functions, which reprices the competitive moat for any infrastructure player not already inside the regulatory tent.

top_signals.title: UBS, Jane Street among firms with combined $75 million in Hyperliquid ETF holdings: Bloomberg
top_signals.summary: Major financial institutions including UBS and Jane Street hold a combined $75 million in Hyperliquid ETF assets. Brazil's Wealth High Governance Asset Management is identified as the largest holder of the 21Shares HYPE fund.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $75 million in institutional ETF holdings reveals that traditional market makers are now using crypto ETFs as balance sheet instruments, which means liquidity provision and price discovery are increasingly happening through regulated wrappers rather than native venues.

top_signals.title: LeBron James teases Polymarket partnership in new social media video
top_signals.summary: NBA star LeBron James has teased a potential partnership with the prediction market platform Polymarket via a social media video. This follows significant betting volume surrounding James' career decisions on prediction platforms.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Celebrity-driven platform partnerships are becoming a primary customer acquisition channel for prediction markets, which underwrites Polymarket's go-to-market efficiency but raises questions about user retention once the marketing event fades.

top_signals.title: Poland upholds crypto bill veto as Zondacrypto scandal widens33m, Poland upholds crypto bill veto as Zondacrypto scandal widensPolish lawmakers failed to overturn a presidential veto of crypto legislation as the Zondacrypto investigation expands and its Estonian operator enters bankruptcy.
top_signals.summary: Polish lawmakers were unable to overturn a presidential veto of a proposed crypto bill. This occurs amidst a widening scandal involving Zondacrypto and the bankruptcy of its Estonian operator.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Poland's veto amid the Zondacrypto scandal shows how enforcement failures in one jurisdiction can cascade into legislative freezes across borders, creating a widening gap between EU member states on crypto regulation that founders must navigate.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin August 2026 Update
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin saw a 25% return in August, driven largely by spot ETFs absorbing approximately $3.9 billion. The price breakout was supported by a prior accumulation regime and a short squeeze, while BTC showed a high correlation with gold as a debasement trade.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $3.9 billion ETF inflow and gold-correlation dynamic suggest BTC is being repriced as a macro debasement asset by institutional allocators, which shifts the relevant benchmark from crypto-native returns to real-asset alternatives.

on_the_radar.title: 🕙 I Want to Trade Stocks in a Market That Doesn't Sleep: SEC Moves to Update Transfer Agent Rules
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC is moving to update transfer agent rules, which could potentially pave the way for tokenized stocks to function as bearer assets. This regulatory shift aims to modernize stock trading to allow for 24/7 market availability.

on_the_radar.title: Tokenized Equities on Solana: From Issuance to Execution
on_the_radar.summary: The article analyzes the growth of tokenized equities on the Solana blockchain, comparing the performance of platforms like Backpack and xStocks. It highlights how Solana's infrastructure and composability provide superior execution and lower fees compared to alternatives like Robinhood Chain.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto firms urge SEC to speed ETF reviews and allow confidential draft filings
on_the_radar.summary: Crypto firms are lobbying the SEC to accelerate the review process for ETFs and permit confidential draft filings. However, firms like Jane Street and Charles Schwab have expressed concerns that such moves could limit market scrutiny and lead to rushed launches.

on_the_radar.title: AMC stock jumps 21% overnight as CEO slams Robinhood over 'outrageous' tokenized shares
on_the_radar.summary: AMC's CEO has criticized Robinhood over the offering of tokenized shares of the company. This follows similar objections from OpenAI regarding the unauthorized tokenization of its equity.

on_the_radar.title: El Salvador’s post-review Bitcoin accumulation used no public funds: IMF
on_the_radar.summary: The IMF has confirmed that El Salvador did not utilize public funds for its Bitcoin accumulation following a review. Additionally, the government has transferred majority control of the Chivo wallet to a private operator.

on_the_radar.title: QuFi launches post-quantum verification platform with Bitcoin testnet proof18m
on_the_radar.summary: QuFi has launched a post-quantum verification platform designed to protect digital assets against future quantum computing threats. The company has demonstrated this capability via a proof-of-concept on the Bitcoin testnet.

on_the_radar.title: Trezor says ShipMonk breach affected another 67,000 customers
on_the_radar.summary: Trezor has announced that an additional 67,000 customers were affected by a data breach at its logistics provider, ShipMonk. The compromised data includes personal identification and shipping details from 2019 to 2021.

on_the_radar.title: Kalshi US visits soar 1,500% as regulatory pressure mounts
on_the_radar.summary: Kalshi has experienced a massive 1,500% surge in US visits during July, reaching 15.4 million. The growth comes amid increasing regulatory pressure and interest in prediction markets.

linkedin_post:
We have watched a16z back a lot of things. A national bank charter for onchain settlement is different. OpenReserve's preliminary OCC approval means the US now has a path for crypto-native institutions to sit at the same regulatory table as JPMorgan and State Street. Not alongside. Inside. That changes what we underwrite when we look at settlement infrastructure.

The $75 million in Hyperliquid ETF holdings from UBS and Jane Street tells the same story from the other direction. Traditional market makers are not experimenting with crypto exposure. They are holding it in regulated wrappers, on balance sheets, alongside every other ETF position. The venue matters less than the wrapper. The wrapper matters less than the regulatory label.

What we are watching now is whether this bifurcates the market or compresses it. If onchain settlement becomes a bank function and ETF holdings become standard practice, the value shifts to whoever owns the regulatory interface. Not the chain. Not the token. The charter.

The test: does OpenReserve's preliminary approval convert to full charter within twelve months, and does any competitor replicate it without the same backing? If yes, this is a sector re-rating. If no, a16z bought a moat.
